sections.heading: Tell Us What the Furnace or AC Is Doing

why: Your AC repair page promises 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year, with someone answering the phone night and day. Your contact page says Monday to Saturday, 7 to 5. Someone whose AC quits on a Sunday can't tell which one is true.

Your homepage links to pages that do not exist: /meditation-retreat-moksha, /retreat-herbal-medicine-101-moksha and /retreat-backpacking-moksha all return "page not found". The homepage code also contains a leftover template line, a second, pasted-in page head titled "Your SEO optimized title". The visible browser title is "ComfortTechs".

On your three product pages, every "Learn more" link goes out to a manufacturer's site: 7 to americanstandardair.com, 3 to mitsubishicomfort.com and 10 to waterfurnace.com. That sends people who are learning about ComfortTechs to manufacturer pages that may list competing dealers. The demo keeps visitors on your own pages.

The homepage H1 is a keyword string, "Comforttechs-Air conditioner, air conditioning repair, ac repair, furnace, …-Lincoln, Nebraska", and 12 of your 16 pages carry the same one, your furnace repair and AC repair pages included. We found no customer testimonials on any page we crawled, while your Google profile has 69 reviews.

So the demo opens with HVAC company in Lincoln, NE, gives furnace repair and AC repair a page each, and puts your own site's strongest facts and your customers' own words side by side, starting with fix it first.

strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page of the demo.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: Where Google learns who you are and where you work.
problems: Your homepage headline is a long string of keywords, so Google can't tell what you want to be found for. Twelve of your 16 pages carry the same one.
Three links on your homepage go to pages that don't exist, and the one we traced is named after a meditation retreat.
The homepage code carries a leftover template line, a second page head titled "Your SEO optimized title".
fixes: A headline that says HVAC company in Lincoln, NE, right at the top.
Every link on the page goes to a page that works, and one clean page head.

cards.title: Furnace Repair
cards.why: When the heat quits, people call the first company they can reach.
problems: Your heating repair page opens with the same string of keywords as your other pages, so it competes with your own homepage for the same search.
fixes: A page that says furnace repair in Lincoln, NE at the top and leads with finding the fix first.

cards.title: AC Repair
cards.why: When the AC quits in a Lincoln summer, people call the first company they can reach.
problems: Your AC repair page opens with the same string of keywords, so it competes with your own homepage and your furnace page.
Its 24-hours-a-day promise doesn't match the hours on your contact page.
fixes: A page that says AC repair in Lincoln, NE at the top and leads with how fast people got an answer.
Hours that match on every page once the owner confirms them.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where a customer with a dead system decides to call.
problems: Your contact page shows two phone numbers, one marked P and one marked C, so a visitor can't tell which to call.
Your Schedule a Service button goes to one page from the homepage and a different page from the maintenance page.
fixes: One number, your address and your email in the first screen, with what to tell us when you call.
A single, plain way to reach you from every page.

closing.text: Your customers already wrote the best copy for it. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame and we'll walk you through this demo and what a full build adds.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your AC repair page says 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, while your contact page says Monday to Saturday, 7 to 5 and closed Sunday, so which hours should Google show?
Your site says since 2007, an owner reply on Google says the company started in 2006, and your footer says copyright 2022, so which year should every listing use?
Your contact page lists 402-465-0000 and a second number, 402-499-4518, marked C, so which one should every listing and every button use?

lead.heading: Why we led with fixing it first
lead.text: The scariest moment for a Lincoln homeowner is hearing you need a whole new system and not knowing if it's true. So the homepage and the furnace page lead with one promise: ComfortTechs looks for the fix before anyone talks about a new system. The AC page leads with how quickly people got an answer, because that is the call on a hot day. The proof for both is already on your Google profile, in your customers' own words, which is why the pages quote them. Please tell us how a replacement conversation actually goes on your end.
